summary.headline: Recreation Commission backs Peninsula Trail CPC funding and selects a 33-space parking design for Fay Memorial Park.
summary.summary: The Southborough Recreation Commission voted to send a letter of support for the Trails Committee's revised Community Preservation Act application to fund a pedestrian bridge along the Peninsula Trail. Commissioners also reviewed parking options for Fay Memorial Park, expressing a clear preference for a 33-space street-parking layout rather than a more costly configuration behind the park. Additionally, the commission reviewed annual safety impact testing for the 9-11 turf field, discussed potential field closures for the upcoming fall Special Town Meeting, and considered renovations at 21 Highland Street.

topics.title: General department updates and 9-11 Field lease
topics.summary: The director provided an update on closing out FY26 finances and reported that the Department of Conservation and Recreation lease invoice for 9-11 Field came in unexpectedly higher by about $1,300, totaling $13,024 instead of the budgeted $10,794. A board member researched the underlying parcel arrangement, noting the 15-year lease runs through roughly 2032 and that town costs are typically offset by state payments in lieu of taxes for watershed land. Staff will verify whether a reserve fund transfer is required or if the cost is balanced through municipal accounting.
key_details: 9-11 Field DCR lease invoice increased by roughly $1,300 to $13,024.
Lease runs for 15 years through approximately 2032.
Town receives approximately $383,000 annually from the state in PILOT watershed payments.
topics.outcome: Staff will follow up with town accounting and the DCR revenue director.

topics.title: Peninsula Trail CPC project update
topics.summary: Trails Committee Chair Kathryn McKee presented an update on the Peninsula Trail, explaining that Phase 1 accessible parking, fencing, and signage are wrapping up. For Phase 2, bids for both a boardwalk and bridge exceeded the budget, so the committee is focusing its Community Preservation Act request on the bridge over the reservoir and rerouting the path onto a natural surface to bypass wetlands. The Recreation Commission voted unanimously to submit a letter of support for the Trails Committee's updated CPC application.
key_details: Phase 1 closed out with unspent CPC funds returned to the general pool after outside grant funding was secured.
Bids for combined boardwalk and bridge exceeded available funds, prompting a bridge-only CPC proposal.
Trails Committee volunteers rerouted the trail around the wetland in early June.
The project connects to the 33-mile Boroughs Loop Trail, the Aqueduct Trail, and the Bay Circuit Trail.
topics.outcome: Voted 3-0 to approve a letter of support for the Trails Committee's CPC application.
topics.why_it_matters: The trail project provides regional trail connectivity and accessible outdoor recreation for Southborough residents using Community Preservation Act funds.

topics.title: Summer programming and department updates
topics.summary: The director shared summer program updates, including camp counselor training and enrollment exceeding targets. Temporary cooling rooms were established in the Woodward School library while air conditioning repairs are scheduled for mid-to-late July. Staff also reported strong registration for the kickoff Family Fun Run and added two new local business sponsors.
key_details: Air conditioning at Woodward School is expected to be repaired in mid-to-late July.
Nearly 80 participants registered for the Family Fun Run kickoff event.
New sponsors include Btone Fitness and Concierge Therapy.
topics.outcome: Informational update; no formal action taken.

topics.title: Fay Memorial Park parking study and CPC application timing
topics.summary: The commission reviewed three design options from the Fay Memorial Park parking study. Commissioners favored Option 2, providing 33 spaces along Central Street and across the road, over Option 3, which proposed 43 spaces but required building a driveway behind the park near the reservoir for an estimated $312,000. Commissioners also debated whether to submit their CPC application for the October 17 Fall Town Meeting or wait for the Annual Town Meeting in spring if fall warrant articles are minimal.
key_details: Option 2 provides 33 total parking spaces including ADA accessible spots along Central Street.
Option 3 was estimated around $312,000 and raised safety and conservation concerns near the reservoir.
DPW installed rapid flashing beacon crosswalks elsewhere in town using a state grant, running roughly $50,000 per unit.
Commissioners leaned toward postponing the park CPC warrant article to spring if the fall meeting agenda is light.
topics.outcome: Commissioners agreed to proceed with Option 2 and will evaluate whether to delay the CPC funding request to spring 2027.
topics.why_it_matters: Parking design and capital improvements at Fay Memorial Park impact user access, pedestrian safety, neighborhood traffic, and town CPC funds.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: Staff noted ongoing recruitment efforts to fill two vacant seats on the Recreation Commission. The commission approved the meeting minutes of May 13 and May 20, 2026, and scheduled their next meeting for late August 2026 before adjourning.
key_details: The commission has two vacant seats.
May 13 and May 20, 2026 meeting minutes were approved unanimously.
Next meeting planned for the week of August 24, 2026.

topics.title: Fall Town Meeting field permit restrictions
topics.summary: The director reported a request originating from the Select Board to consider closing town sports fields on Saturday, October 17, until 12:00 PM to encourage resident attendance at the scheduled 10:00 AM Fall Town Meeting. Commissioners discussed the potential disruption to youth soccer and lacrosse schedules and noted that canceling local games often pushes families to travel out of town rather than attend Town Meeting.
key_details: Fall Town Meeting is scheduled for Saturday, October 17, at 10:00 AM.
Proposed field closure would restrict play until 12:00 PM.
Youth soccer would be the primary group impacted.
topics.outcome: Staff will discuss schedule flexibility with youth sports organizations once permit applications are submitted.

topics.title: 9-11 Field turf impact report
topics.summary: Staff reviewed the annual GMAX impact testing report conducted by RAD Sports for the synthetic turf at 9-11 Field. The field averaged a score of 98, which is within the safe range under 100, though specific high-wear areas like goalmouths reached scores up to 109. RAD Sports advised that if scores approach 110 to 120, the town should consider adding a secondary fall maintenance visit at approximately $2,500 per visit to prolong turf life.
key_details: Overall turf GMAX impact score averaged 98.
High-traffic goalmouth areas scored between 105 and 109.
Additional seasonal maintenance trips cost approximately $2,500 each.
topics.outcome: Commissioners accepted the report and will monitor turf condition.

topics.title: 21 Highland Street building use and improvements
topics.summary: With Youth and Family Services vacating 21 Highland Street in August, the Recreation Department plans to expand its footprint by transforming its current office into an after-school programming room and creating a shared evening meeting space for town boards and committees. The chair also noted discussions from a recent Select Board goal-setting session regarding the potential future sale of the building.
key_details: Youth and Family Services is scheduled to move out in August.
Recreation intends to add an after-school program room and a civic meeting space.
Select Board discussed potential sale of 21 Highland Street during goal-setting sessions.
topics.outcome: Commissioners will tour the facility in August to develop a firm space-use plan.

topics.title: Athletic field net safety discussion
topics.summary: The chair highlighted a recent incident at Trottier Middle School where an owl became tangled in soccer field netting before being successfully rescued. Commissioners discussed the importance of ensuring youth sports leagues take down or bundle nets once their seasons conclude to protect local wildlife.
key_details: An owl was rescued from soccer netting at Trottier Middle School and reunited with its mother.
Staff noted leagues usually take nets down quickly at season end, but vigilance is needed.
topics.outcome: Raised for awareness; no formal policy adopted.
